questions.prompt: Explain why people who eat a lot of large fish may have higher levels of mercury than people who eat mainly vegetables.
questions.modelAnswer: Mercury is not broken down or easily excreted, so it builds up in organisms. Large fish are high in the food chain: they eat many smaller fish, which ate plankton containing mercury, so the concentration increases at each level (biological magnification). People eating large fish are at an even higher level and take in more mercury than those eating plants, which are low in the chain.
